plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-green narrow leaves and dense spikes of small, fragrant flowers. It is widely grown in gardens, in herb borders, and in commercial fields for essential oil production. Bees and butterflies are strongly attracted to it.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Mediterranean native; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: A deciduous shrub with large rounded clusters of showy flowers above broad, glossy leaves. It thrives in partial shade and moist, well-drained soil, and is a fixture of cottage gardens and coastal landscapes.
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in the Azores, the UK, the eastern United States, and Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Flower color depends on soil pH and aluminum availability: acidic soils produce blue blooms, while alkaline soils produce pink ones.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial that rises from muddy pond bottoms, bearing large round leaves and showy, fragrant flowers held above the water. The leaves repel water thanks to a microscopic waxy surface texture.
plants.location: Asia and northern Australia; cultivated in ponds and wetlands from India and China to Japan and the southern United States
plants.funFact: Lotus flowers can regulate their own temperature, staying around 30-35°C (86-95°F) even when the air is much cooler, which helps attract pollinating beetles.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A woody evergreen shrub producing the largest flower head of any protea, with a bowl of silky-tipped petal-like bracts around a central cluster of true flowers. It grows in the fynbos on well-drained, nutrient-poor soils.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering in the cooler months including June
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus, who could change shape, reflecting the wide variety of protea forms.
